What is the University of Science and Technology of Hanoi (USTH)?

USTH, also called Vietnam-France University, is a public university in Hanoi, Vietnam, founded in 2009 under an agreement between Vietnam and France. The official language used for teaching is English.
Who funded the construction of USTH?

USTH was built with funds from the government of Vietnam, the French government, the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology (VAST), the Asian Development Bank, and the USTH Consortium of 42 universities and research organizations in France.
When was USTH established?
USTH was established in 2009 following a decision signed on 12 November 2009 under an intergovernmental agreement between Vietnam and France.
Where is USTH located?
USTH is located in the Hoa Lac Hi-tech Park in Hanoi, Vietnam.
What were the first programs offered by USTH?
The first bachelor and master programs offered by USTH were in Advanced Materials Science and Nanotechnology (AMSN) and Pharmacological and Agronomical Biotechnology (PAB), starting in October 2010.
When did USTH start offering Ph.D. programs?
USTH started offering its first Ph.D. program in August 2014.
How many international joint laboratories are at USTH?
Currently, there are six international joint laboratories at USTH.
When was USTH transferred to VAST?
USTH was transferred to the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology (VAST) on 18 March 2016, as per the Prime Minister's decision.
How many training levels does USTH offer?
USTH offers training programs at three levels: Bachelor, Master, and Ph.D.
What is the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS)?

The European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) is a standard for comparing the academic credit of higher education courses in the European Union, and USTH follows this system in its bachelor programs.
